hot.title: Verifiable On-Policy Distillation
hot.summary: The authors introduce Verifiable On-Policy Distillation (VOPD) for mathematical reasoning, using teacher–verifier agreement within groups of sampled responses to scale teacher guidance across next-token choices. VOPD compares teacher preferences with verified outcomes through a reference-model log-probability shift. In tests of two Qwen3 configurations and eight math benchmarks, it averages 66.38, above OPD and ExOPD, using the student’s top 16 tokens.

hot.title: Sample-Efficient In-Context Adaptation via Sleep
hot.summary: Sleep lets Transformer models refine their key-value cache at chunk boundaries, using recurrent passes over context already read. Rather than add depth to every generated token, the model updates its attention memory periodically, then resumes ordinary decoding. On held-out code, 1.2B-parameter models matched baseline loss with 2.10× fewer context tokens at N=2 and 2.39× at N=4; this measures prefix length, not speed.

hot.title: RoboThink: Let the Agent Think, Let the Policy Act
hot.summary: RoboThink combines a robot policy with an agent that diagnoses problems while the policy acts. It uses task-instruction updates to change goals and learned motion feedback to correct actions. In LIBERO, success rises from 0.09 to 0.87 under constant drift and from 0.42 to 0.84 under random drift; tests are simulation-only, with feedback training on episode-constant drifts.

hot.title: RoboUniverse-10K: Toward the Scaling Era of Agentic Robotics via Real-to-Sim Environments
hot.summary: RoboUniverse-10K turns real manipulation videos into simulated robot-training tasks by having coding agents build scenes, controllers, and verifiers, with an independent agent checking environments. Its 10,807 environments include 10,307 training tasks and 500 held-out tasks. GPT-6.2 Astra reaches 85.8% success on the held-out set, while simulated scenes remain simplified and tasks mostly short-horizon.

hot.title: Recursive Collective Intelligence: Emergence on an Equal-Budget Ladder in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
hot.summary: The authors test when multi-agent communication adds value beyond independent attempts at equal token cost. On HiddenBench, fact forwarding among four Qwen3.8-27B agents reaches 0.959 accuracy, 0.310 above compute-matched pass@n; the full-information agent scores 0.942. On held-out SplitBench tasks, recursive training improves the group’s margin from −0.253 at G0 to +0.159 at G2. These findings are limited to the tested settings.

hot.title: TideSand: Performance-Accurate Sandbox Multiplexing for LLM Agents
hot.summary: TideSand schedules resource-intensive tool calls at execution time, deferring them until sufficient headroom is available, reclaiming memory from sandboxes waiting for inference, and rolling back calls after bursts. Across six model–workload pairs, it reports 3.8–10× higher throughput than strict reservation at similar fidelity, and 7–44% higher fidelity than overcommit at similar throughput. The evaluation was CPU-and-memory only.

hot.title: Attention Latent Feedback
hot.summary: ALF (Attention Latent Feedback) lets each sublayer use the previous token’s outputs at its own and deeper layers, alongside a projected summary of the previous final state. Across three tested MoE sizes, it lowers held-out loss versus standard residual and final-state feedback. On MoE-4.0B, the four-domain average accuracy rises from 45.1% to 47.0% under teacher-forced scoring, not open-ended generation.

hot.title: Pruning Autonomous Driving VLAs: What to Preserve for Reasoning and Action
hot.summary: MoOP compresses Alpamayo-1.5-10B by pruning a vision-language model (VLM) for both Chain-of-Causation explanations and trajectory generation. It ranks units using cross-entropy and flow-matching objectives, retaining VLM units important to either, and selects action-expert MLP channels across denoising steps. With VLM-only pruning at 24.0% total parameter reduction, it scores 68.8% on LingoQA versus 37.0% for FM-only; the dense model scores 73.2%, a difference from MoOP that is not statistically significant.

hot.title: LiveAudio: From Bidirectional to Autoregressive Diffusion for Real-Time Streaming Video-to-Audio Generation
hot.summary: LiveAudio streams video-to-audio by generating short blocks from video already played, using its own generated history and a bidirectional teacher. On VGGSound, DeSync falls from 0.544 after causal ODE distillation to 0.395 after asymmetric DMD, below the teacher’s 0.484. On one NVIDIA A100, it reports 143 ms time to first output and 0.79 real-time factor.

hot.title: Foresight Forcing: Learning Spatial Foresight for Robotic Manipulation
hot.summary: Foresight Forcing trains a robot policy to predict task-relevant spatial changes before generating actions. During training, a frozen 3D vision model supplies correspondence-aligned feature differences, which the policy learns to predict from current images, instructions, and robot state; deployment needs neither future observations nor the teacher. On LIBERO-Plus, it scores 84.5% overall across seven perturbation dimensions, but not every dimension.

hot.title: OWE-Bench: A long-horizon benchmark for measuring real-world engineering
hot.summary: OWE-Bench tests whether agents can judge how well work holds up beyond development examples. Agents use examples, then submit frozen artifacts for scoring on hidden cases; the benchmark compares those scores with development evidence. Across 21 tasks, hidden scores average 17.6 points lower, while models overestimate them by 21 points on average; this gap is not proof of overfitting.

hot.title: Language Model Harnesses can be Compositional Generalizers
hot.summary: The authors train an RLM harness using synthetic traces to improve transfer from shorter tasks to longer contexts. It keeps context outside the root prompt and uses programmatic calls to divide work among smaller inputs. In the same harness, fine-tuned Qwen3.8-27B reaches an eight-benchmark average of 58.5, versus 46.1 for the untrained model, with roughly half inference tokens; transfer is conditional.

hot.title: Beyond Self-Consistency: Recursive Self-Improvement at Test Time
hot.summary: TT-RSI improves mathematical reasoning by feeding each attempt the previous solution and distilling successive refinements into model weights. Across five competition-math benchmarks and Qwen3 models from 1.7B to 8B parameters, it raises average accuracy 13.89 percentage points over Base and 4.79 points over TTPO plus Self-Consistency at equal generated-token budgets. Evaluation covers mathematics, not open-ended tasks.

hot.title: Embo-Harness: Towards Understanding Frontier-Model-as-Policy Harness
hot.summary: Embo-Harness connects a frontier model’s visual reasoning and spatial target selection to robot actions through execution and feedback. It uses absolute end-effector targets, short action chunks, multi-view images, and tools such as VLA refinement. On RoboLab-120 without task-specific fine-tuning, it achieves 83.3% success, versus 57.1% for strongest baseline in the paper’s table; this is not a matched cost comparison.

hot.title: ThinkMorph-SSL: Scaling Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning with Pretext Tasks
hot.summary: ThinkMorph-SSL first trains multimodal models on image-derived restoration traces, then continues with task-specific demonstrations that use intermediate images to answer questions. This two-stage recipe improves average accuracy by 11.33 percentage points over BAGEL think-4k across 12 benchmarks, with gains on all 12. Nine benchmarks lie outside the instruction-tuning task families, but this does not establish that their image sources were unseen.

hot.title: TrialAgentBench: Evaluating AI Agents for Clinical-Trial Analysis and Long-Horizon Drug-Development Decisions
hot.summary: TrialAgentBench evaluates whether agents can estimate clinical-trial treatment effects and make drug-development decisions in simulation. It hides simulated participants’ outcomes under treatment and control, testing analysis on new trials and valuing study-selection and stop-or-advance choices. On 84 TrialEval tasks, Opus 5.5’s mean error was 0.93 standard errors, versus 0.90 for process-aware analysis. On 128 TrialDev programmes, it reached 48% of oracle value; the comparison with the rule-based developer was uncertain, and simulation results do not establish readiness for real development.

hot.title: GameDojo: Benchmarking Real-Time Interactive Agents in Video Games
hot.summary: GameDojo reconstructs 120 boss encounters across 20 games as adjustable tests of real-time interactive skill. It evaluates agents through common controls, varied timing modes, and difficulty levels, and trains a model on controller-generated demonstrations. Fine-tuning improves paused progress, but evaluated models achieve zero wins at medium difficulty in real time; fidelity and transfer to original games remain untested.

hot.title: Unlocking the Power of Loops in Pretrained LLMs with Loop Residuals
hot.summary: LoopRes lets pretrained language models reuse layers for additional computation by giving each reused layer access to recent intermediate results, with cues for their loop positions. On Qwen3-1.7B-Base, it scores 55.8 across seven math and code benchmarks at twice the compute per token of unlooped SFT, versus 43.2 for SFT; general-purpose performance remains untested.

hot.title: ViDiHand2: Unifying Video Diffusion Priors and Hand Geometry for 3D Hand Motion Reconstruction in the Wild
hot.summary: ViDiHand2 reconstructs metric 3D hand motion from egocentric video by fitting hand geometry to camera rays rather than regressing depth from appearance. It combines refined image-joint locations with a posed MANO hand model and confidence-gated fusion. On Gen-HumanEgo, it reduces MPJPE-abs-p from WiLoR’s 56.55 mm to 32.59 mm; the system requires camera intrinsics and runs offline.

hot.title: AlphaDefect: Expert-Level AI for Slay the Spire 2
hot.summary: AlphaDefect uses one learned policy per character for combat and noncombat decisions in Slay the Spire 2. It scores legal actions using player-visible information. Across six characters at Ascension 10, greedy win rates are 62–77%, rising to 68–80% with test-time search. For Ironclad, search increased wins by 5.2 percentage points on v0.113.1, while adding decision-time computation.

likes.title: Language Model Harnesses Can Be Compositional Generalizers
likes.summary: The paper trains a recursive language model harness to handle long tasks by keeping context outside the prompt, using code to inspect it, and delegating smaller queries to model calls. On eight held-out long-context benchmarks, RLM-27B averages 58.5 versus 46.1 for Qwen3.8-27B in the same harness; this is a benchmark-score gain, not a compute or time result.

likes.title: Counterfactual World Models: JEPAs That Reason About "What If"
likes.summary: The authors estimate what an alternative action would have done in the same event by adding the factual model’s predicted change between actions to the observed outcome. This reuses event-specific disturbance without paired counterfactual data or retraining. In simulated HandReach, physical counterfactual R-squared rises from 38.1% to 85.6% after physical readout correction; the result depends on structural conditions.

likes.title: A Claimed Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
likes.summary: Levent Alpöge’s note describes a proposed route to the Riemann Hypothesis, using chained theta lifts to mimic multiplicity in Stepanov’s function-field method, which concerns a different setting. Alpöge reports Claude suggested a chain about √X long for a von Mangoldt sum of length X, and claims the approach extends to GRH; the note offers no readable proof or verification.

likes.title: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer
likes.summary: GLM-5.4 is Z.ai's first flagship model built on a Loop Transformer, which runs a weight-shared block of layers for multiple iterations to add reasoning depth without adding parameters. Rather than pre-training a looped model from scratch, Z.ai adapted the pre-trained GLM-5 base through continued training, looping 28 layers for two iterations at 750B scale. The post frames the model as the start of "Generalized Coding", where code generation extends to video, CAD, games, and 3D.

likes.title: Composable Soft-Prompt Distillation of RL Experts: Toward Continual Post-Training
likes.summary: CSPD turns reinforcement-learning specialists into independently trained soft prompts, keeping the pre-reinforcement-learning backbone frozen and concatenating selected prompts at inference. In a four-domain test with a Qwen3-4B student, the composed prompts raised the average score from 50.41 to 67.83, compared with 67.79 for MOPD. This result covers four tested domains, not broader scaling.

likes.title: Feedback Shortcut: Speculative Decoding for Latent Feedback Transformers
likes.summary: Feedback Shortcut enables speculative decoding for latent-feedback Transformers. It aligns multi-token prediction head states as feedback stand-ins, then recomputes pending positions during the next verification call. For a 780M model with three heads, one correction, and batch size 1, it reports 0.8287 BPB versus 0.8288 for exact decoding, and 2.75× throughput; this is single-GPU steady-state serving, not exact output equivalence.

likes.title: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights
likes.summary: The authors graft a deterministic arithmetic circuit into pretrained model weights, enabling signed addition, subtraction, and multiplication without gradient updates, labeled examples, or runtime tool calls. Scale-robust circuit primitives and tokenizer-aligned emission let the language model resume after the answer. On Arith-1200, BF16 grafts reach 99.17% on Granite 4.2 3B and 100.00% on Qwen 3.5 4B, within the suite’s tested formats.

likes.title: Perplexity and Intelligence

likes.title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
likes.summary: Mind2Act World tests whether robots use memory, execution, and feedback across related simulated tabletop tasks. It separates memory-focused Mind tasks, action-focused Act tasks, and workflows where outcomes guide later decisions. GPT-6 Astra succeeds on 52.7% of Mind episodes, 39.0% of Act episodes, and 12.0% of Mind2Act episodes. These task-set rates do not isolate composition as the cause, and physical-robot transfer remains unmeasured.

likes.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
likes.summary: Depth Pro 2 estimates metric depth from images and video by processing frames jointly at native resolution with within-frame and cross-frame attention. In zero-shot comparisons, H+ ranks first for video metric-depth accuracy, boundary sharpness, and temporal consistency. On Sintel with predicted intrinsics, H+ reaches 41.4% δ1 versus 37.0% for UniDepthV2-L; rankings summarize separate measures, and results vary by model size.

likes.title: Frontier Models Need Only One Text to Unmask Its Human or AI Author
likes.summary: The authors test whether frontier models can identify human authors from one text and a zero-shot prompt without tools, candidate lists, or reference samples. On private ICML 2020 reviews, Claude Fable 5.2 correctly named reviewers for 55.4% of 15,136 reviews. Results vary with familiarity; private review authors’ other writing may still have been known to the model.

likes.title: Jeveration: System One Models Now Generate
likes.summary: Jeveration generates images in one forward pass by predicting 128 discrete image codes together and decoding them. A shared random state is supplied to every code position to help coordinate choices. At 512 × 512, it reports 77.8 ms and a GenEval overall score of 0.74, versus 94.1 ms and 0.63 for four-step Show-o Turbo-512 in a same-resolution comparison.

likes.title: Posterior Matching Distillation
likes.summary: Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD) trains a stochastic few-step image generator to preserve multiple plausible clean images for the same noisy input. It matches exponentially weighted student predictions to shifted-input targets from a frozen teacher under Gaussian corruption. On four-step FLUX.2 [klein] 4B, PMD reaches Vendi 3.3708 versus 2.4104 for SMD, with FID 24.12 versus 24.58 for the base model.

likes.title: MAWAM: A Multi-Agent World-Action Model for Coordinated Manipulation
likes.summary: MAWAM predicts each robot’s action chunk and future private camera views jointly, using cross-agent attention while preserving separate robot streams. Robots execute actions, observe the scene, and replan. Across three real-robot tasks, it averaged 67.8% success versus 48.9% for a MA-VLA reimplementation; it averaged 90.3% across eight simulated tasks. These results concern fixed teams of at most four agents.

likes.title: Grana: Compositional Reward Modeling for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
likes.summary: Grana predicts progress in long-horizon robot manipulation by selecting an unfinished subtask from user-supplied descriptions and estimating local progress from multiview observations. It combines that estimate with credit for earlier completed subtasks. On 50 held-out tasks, it achieves 0.180 RMSE versus 0.227 for RoboMeter without target-task labels or fine-tuning; this supports transfer, not universal performance.

likes.title: Unified Law for Visual Tasks (The Four Laws of Computer Vision)
likes.summary: The authors propose World Snapshot Models, which treat visual tasks as directed condition-to-target mappings through task-specific routes in a shared, frozen image generator. For structured outputs, Modality Tunneling Attention produced structured RGB-to-normal output at 250 optimizer updates, versus 4,750 for a matched Native Joint Attention baseline. The study evaluates 1,148 dense mappings, not every visual task or world attribute.
